s.note: the headwaiter's grand salad routine at the restaurant
s.how: Tear 1 bread roll into chunks, toss with 2 tbsp olive oil and 1 crushed garlic clove and bake at 190C for 10 minutes. Cook 4 eggs for 7 minutes, cool and halve. Mash 4 anchovies with 1 garlic clove, then whisk in 1 tsp Dijon, the juice of 1 lemon, 4 tbsp mayonnaise and 30g grated parmesan. Tear 1 cos and 1 butter lettuce into a big bowl, toss with the dressing and croutons and top with the eggs and more parmesan.

Bring 250ml water, 100g butter and a pinch of salt to the boil. Beat in 150g plain flour until it forms a ball and cook 1 minute. Cool 5 minutes, then beat in 4 eggs one at a time, then 120g grated gruyère, 1 tsp Dijon and a pinch of cayenne. Pipe 24 small mounds on lined trays, sprinkle with more gruyère and bake at 200C for 22 minutes until puffed and golden.

m.n: Easter Sunday roast lamb with mint sauce
m.note: Easter Sunday lunch in New York
m.how: Make small cuts all over a 2kg lamb leg and push in slivers of 4 garlic cloves and rosemary sprigs. Rub with oil and salt and roast at 190C for 1 hour 30 minutes for medium. Rest 20 minutes. Roast 1.2kg parboiled potatoes in oil alongside. For mint sauce, chop a bunch of mint with 1 tbsp sugar, add 3 tbsp boiling water and 4 tbsp malt vinegar. Serve with 300g buttered peas.

w.n: Hot cross bun bread and butter pudding
w.how: Butter 6 halved hot cross buns and layer them in a baking dish. Whisk 3 eggs, 400ml milk, 200ml cream, 60g caster sugar, 1 tsp vanilla and the zest of 1 orange and pour over. Stand 15 minutes. Bake at 170C for 35 minutes until golden and just set. Warm 3 tbsp apricot jam with a splash of water and brush over the top. Serve warm with cream.

d.note: the Easter bonnets on Fifth Avenue
d.how: In a punch bowl, mix 500ml cranberry juice, 300ml pink grapefruit juice and 200g sliced strawberries and chill 30 minutes. Add plenty of ice. For the adults, top glasses with sparkling wine. For everyone else, top with lemonade. Garnish each glass with a strawberry on the rim.
